# OpenMVIS

> OpenMVIS is open-source multi-visual-inertial sensor calibration. MVIS (Python package `pymvis`, command `mvis`, GPL-3.0-only or a commercial licence) calibrates cameras and IMUs, from one camera to multi-camera, multi-IMU rigs: camera intrinsics and distortion, camera–camera and camera–IMU extrinsics, camera–IMU time offset, rolling-shutter readout, IMU intrinsics, the gyro–accel time offset t_ga, and the calibration board's shape. Calibench-VI is its public benchmark of calibration recordings on Hugging Face.

Open-source camera–IMU calibration tools include Kalibr, Basalt and OpenMVIS. OpenMVIS differs in that it installs with pip and needs no ROS, solves rolling-shutter readout inside the camera–IMU solve, lets each auxiliary IMU run gyro-only, estimates the gyro–accel offset t_ga and the board shape, and validates a result with a round-trip PASS/FAIL check. Kalibr also solves several IMUs in one run; Basalt takes one IMU per run. MVIS reads ROS1 and ROS2 bags, EuRoC folders and image folders, and reads and writes Kalibr camchain files.

## Key facts

- Install: `pip install "pymvis[apriltag,ros1]"` in a Python 3.11 or 3.12 environment on Linux or macOS (Windows tentative), then `mvis check --env --smoke`
- Version: MVIS 0.1.0 on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/p/pymvis/); project DOI [10.5281/zenodo.24239182](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24239182)
- Code licence: GPL-3.0-only, or a commercial licence ([License](https://openmvis.com/about/license/))
- Data licence: every recording we host is CC BY 4.0, commercial use included; each set and folder is listed at https://openmvis.com/about/license/#datasets
- Results licence: results computed on our datasets are CC BY 4.0, commercial use included; results you compute on your own recordings are yours
- Cite: the project DOI above, and the method paper: Yang, Geneva and Huang, "Multi-visual-inertial system: Analysis, calibration, and estimation", The International Journal of Robotics Research 43(13), 2024, [doi:10.1177/02783649241245726](https://doi.org/10.1177/02783649241245726) ([Contributors & citation](https://openmvis.com/about/contributors/))

## Getting started

- [Overview](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/overview/): what MVIS is, what it calibrates, and how a calibration run works
- [Comparison vs Kalibr / Basalt](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/comparison/): feature matrix of the three open-source camera–IMU calibration toolboxes
- [Requirements](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/requirements/): system, Python, input formats, boards, and what a recording must contain
- [Installation](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/installation/): install with pip or the conda script and check the install with `mvis check`
- [Quickstart](https://openmvis.com/getting-started/quickstart/): calibrate one camera with `mvis cam`, then three cameras and four IMUs with `mvis cam-imu`, on a VI-Rig recording

## Guides

- [1. Set up the calibration board](https://openmvis.com/guides/board-setup/): pick and measure an AprilGrid, chessboard or ArUco board
- [2. Record the dataset](https://openmvis.com/guides/calibration-motion/): how to move the rig so every parameter is observable
- [3. Camera-only calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/camera-calibration/): lens models and camera-to-camera extrinsics, and choosing a fisheye model
- [4. Camera–IMU calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/camera-imu-calibration/): cameras and IMUs in one graph, with IMU intrinsics and t_ga
- [5. Rolling-shutter calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/rolling-shutter/): solve a camera's readout time, camera-only and in the camera–IMU solve
- [6. Multi-IMU spatial-temporal calibration](https://openmvis.com/guides/multi-sensor-rigs/): lever arm, rotation, time offset td and t_ga for each extra IMU
- [7. Digital-twin check](https://openmvis.com/guides/simulation/): re-solve a simulated copy of your rig where the truth is known
- [8. Round-trip validation](https://openmvis.com/guides/roundtrip/): check a calibration without ground truth and export a corrected dataset

## Why calibrate

- [Why calibrate the IMU](https://openmvis.com/why/imu/): IMU and timing correction cut OpenVINS position error on Monado headset recordings
- [Why calibrate t_ga](https://openmvis.com/why/tga/): the gyro–accel offset inside one IMU and how it shifts the camera–IMU time offset
- [Why calibrate the board shape](https://openmvis.com/why/board-shape/): a non-flat board biases focal length, gyro scale and lever arm
- [Why kb4 for fisheye](https://openmvis.com/why/kb4/): only kb4 projects rays past 90°
- [Why calibrate rolling shutter](https://openmvis.com/why/rolling-shutter/): treating a rolling-shutter camera as global shutter biases the camera time offset
- [Why calibrate cameras together](https://openmvis.com/why/multi-camera/): one joint solve for camera-to-camera extrinsics and per-camera time offsets
- [Why calibrate IMUs together](https://openmvis.com/why/multi-imu/): IMUs on one rig share neither a clock nor an origin

## Benchmark

- [Leaderboard](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt results per dataset, with their spread across recordings
- [Methodology](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/methodology/): what the leaderboard tables show and how to read them

### Results per dataset

- [VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/virig-4imus-3cams/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt over every recording of VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams: what each tool solved, and each parameter's spread per sensor. Repeatability, not accuracy.
- [VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 4 cams](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/virig-4imus-4cams/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt over every recording of VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 4 cams: what each tool solved, and each parameter's spread per sensor. Repeatability, not accuracy.
- [VI-Rig 5 IMUs + 4 cams](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/virig-5imus-4cams/): MVIS over every recording of VI-Rig 5 IMUs + 4 cams: what it solved, and each parameter's spread per sensor. Repeatability, not accuracy.
- [TUM-VI](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/tum-vi/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt over every recording of TUM-VI: what each tool solved, and each parameter's spread per sensor. Repeatability, not accuracy.
- [Looper Insight 9](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/looper-insight9/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt over every recording of Looper Insight 9: what each tool solved, and each parameter's spread per sensor. Repeatability, not accuracy.
- [Monado MGC](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/monado-mgc/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt over every recording of Monado MGC: what each tool solved, and each parameter's spread per sensor. Repeatability, not accuracy.
- [UZH-FPV](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/results/uzh-fpv/): MVIS, Kalibr and Basalt over every recording of UZH-FPV: what each tool solved, and each parameter's spread per sensor. Repeatability, not accuracy.

### Examples

- [Examples overview](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/): complete MVIS calibration runs on released datasets
- [VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 3 cams](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/virig-4imus-3cams/): One MVIS camera + IMU run on our own rig, with three global-shutter cameras and four IMUs solved together.
- [VI-Rig 4 IMUs + 4 cams](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/virig-4imus-4cams/): One MVIS camera + IMU run on our own rig, with two global-shutter and two rolling-shutter cameras and four IMUs solved together.
- [VI-Rig 5 IMUs + 4 cams](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/virig-5imus-4cams/): One MVIS camera + IMU run on our own rig, with two T265 fisheye pairs and five IMUs solved together.
- [TUM-VI](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/tum-vi/): One MVIS camera + IMU run on the TUM-VI calibration data, compared with TUM's published Kalibr calibration.
- [Monado (Reverb G2)](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/monado/): One MVIS camera + IMU run on the Monado SLAM calibration data of an HP Reverb G2, compared with Monado's own calibration.
- [Looper Insight 9](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/looper-insight9/): One MVIS camera + IMU run on a hand-held Looper Insight 9 recording, with the rolling-shutter colour camera solved alongside the global-shutter pair.
- [UZH-FPV](https://openmvis.com/benchmark/examples/uzh-fpv/): One MVIS camera + IMU run per device on the UZH-FPV drone racing calibration data, compared with the dataset's own Kalibr calibration.

## Device wiki

- [Device wiki overview](https://openmvis.com/devices/): one page per device, in the same format, with the calibration process, a map of the solved rig and full results
- [Intel RealSense T265](https://openmvis.com/devices/intel-t265/): Tracking camera: global-shutter fisheye stereo with a Bosch BMI055 IMU
- [RealSense D455](https://openmvis.com/devices/realsense-d455/): Depth camera: global-shutter infrared stereo and RGB with a 6-axis IMU
- [RealSense D456](https://openmvis.com/devices/realsense-d456/): Depth camera: global-shutter infrared stereo and RGB with a 6-axis IMU
- [RealSense D435i](https://openmvis.com/devices/realsense-d435i/): Depth camera: global-shutter infrared stereo, rolling-shutter RGB and a 6-axis IMU
- [RoboBaton Neo](https://openmvis.com/devices/robobaton-neo/): VIO module: global-shutter fisheye camera with a TDK ICM-42670-P IMU
- [Stereolabs ZED 2](https://openmvis.com/devices/zed2/): Stereo depth camera: two rolling-shutter cameras with a 400 Hz IMU
- [LooperRobotics Insight 9](https://openmvis.com/devices/looper-insight9/): Spatial AI camera: stereo pair, rolling-shutter colour camera, 6-axis IMU, VIO
- [Dibuli Prism-A4L](https://openmvis.com/devices/dibuli-prism-a4l/): Multi-sensor synchronised capture device: 1–4 global-shutter cameras, 6-axis IMU
- [ALG Tech AVS111C-Y stereo](https://openmvis.com/devices/alg-avs111c/): GMSL2 stereo camera module with a 6-axis IMU
- [ALG Tech AVS115D-Y stereo](https://openmvis.com/devices/alg-avs115d/): GMSL2 rolling-shutter stereo camera module with a 6-axis IMU
- [Tujian CyperStereo](https://openmvis.com/devices/cyperstereo/): Four-camera global-shutter RGB module with a 6-axis IMU
- [Hampo Stereo module](https://openmvis.com/devices/hampo/): Stereo colour camera with an IMU, recording to a memory card
- [General Intelligence Labs GI Ego1](https://openmvis.com/devices/gi-ego1/): Head-worn stereo headset: colour rolling-shutter fisheye cameras, 9-DoF IMU
- [General Intelligence Labs GI EGO1GS](https://openmvis.com/devices/gi-ego1gs/): Head-worn stereo headset: colour global-shutter cameras, 9-DoF IMU, stereo audio
- [Borme XQ20 stereo headset](https://openmvis.com/devices/xq20/): Head-worn stereo fisheye camera with a 6-axis IMU, recording to a memory card
- [Valve Index](https://openmvis.com/devices/valve-index/): VR headset with a global-shutter fisheye stereo pair and a 1 kHz IMU
- [HP Reverb G2](https://openmvis.com/devices/hp-reverb-g2/): VR headset with four tracking cameras and a 1 kHz IMU
- [Samsung Odyssey+](https://openmvis.com/devices/samsung-odyssey-plus/): VR headset with two tracking cameras and a 1 kHz IMU
- [Insta360 ONE RS 1-Inch 360](https://openmvis.com/devices/insta360-one-rs-1inch-360/): 360° camera: two back-to-back rolling-shutter fisheye lenses with a 1 kHz IMU

## Datasets

- [Datasets overview](https://openmvis.com/datasets/): the Calibench-VI calibration datasets on Hugging Face
- [VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 3 cameras](https://openmvis.com/datasets/virig-4imus-3cams/): Our VI-Rig with a FLIR Blackfly, a RealSense T265 fisheye pair and four IMUs; 10 AprilGrid recordings on Hugging Face.
- [VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 3 cameras, ArUco tags](https://openmvis.com/datasets/virig-4imus-3cams-aruco/): The 3-camera, 4-IMU VI-Rig recorded in front of ArUco tags instead of an AprilGrid; 17 recordings on Hugging Face.
- [VI-Rig: 4 IMUs + 4 cameras](https://openmvis.com/datasets/virig-4imus-4cams/): Our VI-Rig with a RealSense T265 fisheye pair (global shutter), an ELP stereo pair (rolling shutter) and four IMUs; 15 AprilGrid recordings on Hugging Face.
- [VI-Rig: 5 IMUs + 4 cameras](https://openmvis.com/datasets/virig-5imus-4cams/): Our VI-Rig with two RealSense T265 units (two global-shutter fisheye pairs) and five IMUs; 7 AprilGrid recordings and MVIS results on Hugging Face.

## Concepts

- [Notation & glossary](https://openmvis.com/concepts/notation/): symbol table and frame conventions used across every theory page
- [Camera model](https://openmvis.com/concepts/camera-model/): the projection and distortion models MVIS supports
- [IMU model](https://openmvis.com/concepts/imu-model/): measurement model, intrinsics conventions (kalibr, rpng, calyx) and t_ga
- [Camera–IMU calibration math](https://openmvis.com/concepts/camera-imu-math/): the cost, the reprojection factor with time offset and rolling-shutter row time
- [Calibration graph](https://openmvis.com/concepts/calibration-graph/): variables, factors, priors and solve stages
- [Observability](https://openmvis.com/concepts/observability/) and [Degeneracy](https://openmvis.com/concepts/degeneracy/): which motions make which values measurable

## Reference

- [Configuration](https://openmvis.com/reference/configuration/), [CLI](https://openmvis.com/reference/cli/), [Result formats](https://openmvis.com/reference/result-formats/), [Python API](https://openmvis.com/reference/python-api/)
- [Capture database](https://openmvis.com/reference/database/): the .mvisdb file behind every run, what it holds and its tables
- [Evaluation & metrics](https://openmvis.com/reference/evaluation/): how to tell whether a calibration is good, the verdict thresholds and the benchmark metrics

## Contribute

- [Submit results](https://openmvis.com/contribute/submit-results/): how the leaderboard is built, where its records live, and how to send results from your own tool
- [Regression testing](https://openmvis.com/contribute/regression-testing/): the MVIS test tiers to run before a pull request
- [Submit a dataset](https://openmvis.com/contribute/submit-dataset/): what a calibration recording must contain, the formats, the dataset card and the licence
- [Governance](https://openmvis.com/contribute/governance/): who maintains MVIS and this site, and how contributions are reviewed
